name: Inverse Head and Shoulders
description: A three-trough formation where the middle trough (head) is the lowest, flanked by two higher troughs (shoulders) of approximately equal depth. It signals the exhaustion of a downtrend and a likely reversal to the upside.
formation_rules: Price must be in a confirmed downtrend prior to pattern formation
Left shoulder forms as price drops to a low, then bounces
Head forms as price drops to a lower low than the left shoulder, then bounces back to a similar peak level
Right shoulder forms as price drops to a low roughly equal to the left shoulder, then bounces
A neckline is drawn connecting the two peaks between the shoulders and head
The right shoulder low must be higher than the head and approximately equal to or higher than the left shoulder
The two peaks (neckline points) should be at a similar price level, within 3% of each other
volume_rules: Volume is typically highest on the left shoulder decline, lower on the head decline, and lowest on the right shoulder decline. Volume should expand noticeably on the rally phases. A volume expansion of at least 1.5x average on the neckline breakout candle is required for confirmation.
measured_target_method: Measure the vertical distance from the bottom of the head to the neckline. Project that distance upward from the neckline breakout point to get the minimum price target.
confirmation_conditions: Price closes above the neckline on a daily or weekly candle
Breakout candle volume is at least 1.5x the 20-period average volume
A retest of the neckline from above followed by a bounce confirms the breakout
RSI or MACD showing bullish divergence at the head or right shoulder strengthens the signal
invalidation_conditions: Price reclaims and closes below the neckline after the breakout
The right shoulder forms a low that is deeper than the head, invalidating the structure
Volume surges significantly on a sell-off back below the neckline
Price closes below the right shoulder low before a neckline break occurs

agent_rules.rule: Breakout is confirmed only when the closing price of a candle is strictly above the neckline; wicks above the neckline without a close do not constitute confirmation.
Volume on the breakout candle must be >= 1.5x the 20-period simple moving average of volume; if not met, treat the break as unconfirmed and wait for the next candle.
Pattern is invalidated when price produces a daily close below the neckline after a confirmed breakout; cancel all bullish targets and reassess bias.
Measured target = neckline breakout price + (neckline price at head's time - head low price); flag the target as reached when price touches or crosses it intraday.
